stem.text: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, and carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, both have $M_\text{r} = 28$.
What could be responsible for this difference in boiling points?

A.text: $\text{CO}$ molecules have a permanent dipole; the $\text{N}_2$ molecules are **not** polar.

B.text: $\text{N}_2$ has $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonding; $\text{CO}$ has $\sigma$ bonding only.

C.text: $\text{N}_2$ has a strong $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond; $\text{CO}$ has a $\text{C=O}$ bond.

D.text: The $\text{CO}$ molecule has more electrons than the $\text{N}_2$ molecule.
